targetTexts.1: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor does not befit a fool.
targetTexts.2: Like a fluttering sparrow or darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
targetTexts.3: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!
targetTexts.4: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be like him.
targetTexts.5: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
targetTexts.6: Like cutting off one’s own feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.
targetTexts.7: Like lame legs hanging limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
targetTexts.8: Like binding a stone into a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.
targetTexts.9: Like a thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
targetTexts.10: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or passerby.
targetTexts.11: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
targetTexts.12: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
targetTexts.13: The slacker says, “A lion is in the road! A fierce lion roams the public square!”
targetTexts.14: As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his bed.
targetTexts.15: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.
targetTexts.16: The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.
targetTexts.17: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
targetTexts.18: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows,
targetTexts.19: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
targetTexts.20: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
targetTexts.21: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
targetTexts.22: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
targetTexts.23: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
targetTexts.24: A hateful man disguises himself with his speech, but he lays up deceit in his heart.
targetTexts.25: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
targetTexts.26: Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
targetTexts.27: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
targetTexts.28: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
